note.title: Passé composé
note.overview: This lesson contains 88 enabled questions. It teaches Passé composé through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Passé composé.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Passé composé = present auxiliary + past participle.
Movement verbs in the taught bank use être.
With être, add -e, -s or -es when required.
Time phrases such as hier and la semaine dernière signal completed past.
Some movement verbs use avoir when they take a direct object.

workedExamples.why: The teacher coverage gives aller → allé (to go). In the passé composé, the past participle follows the correct auxiliary.

workedExamples.why: The teacher coverage gives partir → parti (to leave). In the passé composé, the past participle follows the correct auxiliary.

commonMistakes: Choosing avoir for a taught être movement verb.
A past participle is not the whole tense: a full sentence also needs the subject and auxiliary.
A small article or ending can change the grammar even when the main vocabulary is recognisable.
